PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}}

{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to Shotokuen File:Artillery Sentry Box of Asahikawa 7th Regiment.JPG|Artillery sentry box of the Asahikawa 7th Regiment File:Birthplace of the artillery to defend the northern land.JPG|"Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument File:Cenotaph of nurses in Sakhalin at Shotokuen.JPG|Memorial for nurses in Sakhalin File:Monument to burning the Ensign of 26th Infantry Regiment.JPG|26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial File:Monument of Toshiro Matsumoto.JPG|Toshiro Matsumoto Memorial File:Monument to Nikolayevsk Incident at Shotokuen.JPG|Nikolaevsk Incident Monument File:Monument to Brave Souls of Honorable Dead in Attu at Shotokuen.JPG|Attu Island Monument File:Monument to Heroic Souls of the Battle of Khalkhin Gol at Shotokuen.JPG|Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument File:Chûkon-hi at Shotokuen.JPG|Chukon-hi and Tondenhei Memorial File:Monuments to Yamahana Shrine at Shotokuen.JPG|Monuments for Yamahana Shrine File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Mereyon Island at Shotokuen.JPG|Mereyon {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}}
'''Taga Hall'''
{{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}}

{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to Shotokuen File:Artillery Sentry Box of Asahikawa 7th Regiment.JPG|Artillery sentry box of the Asahikawa 7th Regiment File:Birthplace of the artillery to defend the northern land.JPG|"Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument File:Cenotaph of nurses in Sakhalin at Shotokuen.JPG|Memorial for nurses in Sakhalin File:Monument to burning the Ensign of 26th Infantry Regiment.JPG|26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial File:Monument of Toshiro Matsumoto.JPG|Toshiro Matsumoto Memorial File:Monument to Nikolayevsk Incident at Shotokuen.JPG|Nikolaevsk Incident Monument File:Monument to Brave Souls of Honorable Dead in Attu at Shotokuen.JPG|Attu Island Monument File:Monument to Heroic Souls of the Battle of Khalkhin Gol at Shotokuen.JPG|Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument File:Chûkon-hi at Shotokuen.JPG|Chukon-hi and Tondenhei Memorial File:Monuments to Yamahana Shrine at Shotokuen.JPG|Monuments for Yamahana Shrine File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Mereyon Island at Shotokuen.JPG|Mereyon Island Cenotaph File:Cenotaph of North Kuril at Shotokuen.JPG|Northern Kurils Cenotaph File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Southern Region at Shotokuen.JPG|Southern Region War Dead Cenotaph File:Monument to Heroic Souls of All Hokkaido Navy at Shotokuen.JPG|Monument for Hokkaido Naval War Dead File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Okinawa at Shotokuen.JPG|Okinawa War Dead Cenotaph == See Also == * [[Controversies PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. Pathway |location = {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Minami 15-jo Nishi (Sapporo)|ja|南15条西5丁目}} 1 |rank degrees = 43 | type minutes = 2 | type seconds = 26.5 | N/S = N |longitude degrees = 141 | longitude minutes = 21 | longitude seconds = 10.5 | E/W = E |map country code = JP |map = Sapporo2 |Deities = '''main hall'''
{{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}}
{{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}}
{{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}}
{{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}}
'''Taga Hall'''
{{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to Shotokuen File:Artillery Sentry Box of Asahikawa 7th Regiment.JPG|Artillery sentry box of the Asahikawa 7th Regiment File:Birthplace of the artillery to defend the northern land.JPG|"Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument File:Cenotaph of nurses in Sakhalin at Shotokuen.JPG|Memorial for nurses in Sakhalin File:Monument to burning the Ensign of 26th Infantry Regiment.JPG|26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial File:Monument of Toshiro Matsumoto.JPG|Toshiro Matsumoto Memorial File:Monument to Nikolayevsk Incident at Shotokuen.JPG|Nikolaevsk Incident Monument File:Monument to Brave Souls of Honorable Dead in Attu at Shotokuen.JPG|Attu Island Monument File:Monument to Heroic Souls of the Battle of Khalkhin Gol at Shotokuen.JPG|Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument File:Chûkon-hi at Shotokuen.JPG|Chukon-hi and Tondenhei Memorial File:Monuments to Yamahana Shrine at Shotokuen.JPG|Monuments for Yamahana Shrine File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Mereyon Island at Shotokuen.JPG|Mereyon Island Cenotaph File:Cenotaph of North Kuril at Shotokuen.JPG|Northern Kurils Cenotaph File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Southern Region at Shotokuen.JPG|Southern Region War Dead Cenotaph File:Monument to Heroic Souls of All Hokkaido Navy at Shotokuen.JPG|Monument for Hokkaido Naval War Dead File:Cenotaph of War Dead in Okinawa at Shotokuen.JPG|Okinawa War Dead Cenotaph == See Also! == * The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} |Shrine rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道}}. '''Taga Hall'''
{{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神}}
