The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=draft|12=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=draft|12=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|12=draft|12=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|12=draft|12=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|12=draft|12=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft|12=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|12=draft|12=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|12=draft|12=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=draft|12=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=draft|12=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=draft|12=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|12=draft|12=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=draft|12=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=draft|12=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=draft|12=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|12=draft|12=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|12=draft|12=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=draft|12=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=draft|12=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=draft|12=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|12=draft|12=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|12=draft|12=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|12=draft|12=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft|12=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|12=draft|12=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|12=draft|12=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=draft|12=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=draft|12=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=draft|12=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=draft|12=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|12=draft|12=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=draft|12=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to Shotokuen File:Artillery Sentry Box of Asahikawa 7th Regiment.JPG|Artillery sentry box of the Asahikawa 7th Regiment File:Birthplace of the artillery to defend the northern land.JPG|"Birthplace of the In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to Shotokuen File:Artillery Sentry Box of Asahikawa 7th Regiment.JPG|Artillery sentry box of the Asahikawa 7th Regiment File:Birthplace of the artillery to defend the northern land.JPG|"Birthplace of the 耳早立雄大神 |社格 = |創建 = [[1879年]]（[[明治]]12年） |本殿 = |別名 = |例祭 = [[7月6日]] |神事 = }} '''札幌護国神社'''（さっぽろごこくじんじゃ、{{旧字体|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}）は、[[北海道]][[札幌市]][[中央区 (札幌市)|中央区]]にある[[神社]]。[[護国神社]]の一つである。 [[1879年]]（明治12年）に、[[西南戦争]]で戦没した[[屯田兵]]の[[霊]]を祀るために建立され[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm 神社紹介] – 札幌護国神社公式ホームページ、2012年10月2日閲覧。、以後各戦争における戦死者の霊を[[合祀]]してきたが、[[1949年]]（昭和24年）9月より[[多賀大社]]の祭神を[[勧請]]し、次いで[[1971年]]（昭和46年）9月に[[山鼻]]の[[鎮守神|鎮守]]であった山鼻神社の祭神を合祀し、現在に至る。 そのため、同社は創建当初からの祭神を祀る本殿と、多賀大社より勧請した神々および旧・山鼻神社の祭神を祀る'''多賀殿'''（[[多賀神社]]）から構成される。 == 祭神 == ; 本殿 * 北海道開拓祭神 * 各戦役戦没祭神 * 公共殉職祭神 * 其他特殊祭神 ** 本殿の祭神数は、[[2011年]]（[[平成]]23年）現在で25543柱。 ; 多賀殿 * [[伊邪那岐大神]] * [[伊邪那美大神]] * [[相殿]][[奉斎]]（旧・山鼻神社祭神） ** [[天照大御神]] ** [[大山祗大神]] ** [[天満宮大神]] ** [[耳早立雄大神]] == 沿革 == * [[1879年]]（[[明治]]12年） – 現在の札幌市北区北6条西7丁目に屯田兵招魂碑が建てられ、'''札幌忠魂社'''と称される。 * [[1911年]]（明治44年）2月 – [[中島公園]]に移る。 * [[1922年]]（[[大正]]11年）[[7月1日]] – '''札幌招魂社'''と改称する。 * [[1933年]]（[[昭和]]8年） – 現在地に社殿が建てられる。 * [[1939年]]（昭和14年）[[4月1日]] – '''札幌護国神社'''と改称し、内務大臣指定護国神社となる[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html 札幌護国神社] – 北海道神社庁、2012年10月2日閲覧。。 * [[1946年]]（昭和21年） ** [[4月30日]] – [[神社本庁]]の所属となる。 ** [[12月12日]] – '''札幌彰徳神社'''と改称する（日本の独立承認後、札幌護國神社に復称）。 * [[1949年]]（昭和24年）9月 – 多賀大社より祭神を勧請し、多賀殿が建立する。 * [[1968年]]（昭和43年） – 火災により社殿が焼失する。 * [[1970年]]（昭和45年） – 社殿が再建される。 * [[1971年]]（昭和46年）9月 – 山鼻神社の祭神を多賀殿に合祀する。 * [[1972年]]（昭和47年）[[2月3日]] – [[昭和天皇]]・[[香淳皇后]]が親拝する。 == 彰徳苑 == 境内の一角には、戦没者慰霊碑を中心に数多くの碑が集められた「彰徳苑」がある。 ; 屯田兵招魂碑 : [[1878年]]（明治11年）7月、[[西南戦争]]で没した[[屯田兵]]のために建てられた物で、札幌市内に現存する最古の碑と考えられる{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.1}}。 : 当初は[[偕楽園 (札幌市)|偕楽園]]にあった。[[1907年]]（明治40年）12月、[[日露戦争]]における札幌連隊区管内からの戦死者を合祀し、[[中島公園|中島遊園地]]に移転。[[1933年]]（昭和8年）、招魂社境内に再移転した{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.1}}。 ; [[忠魂碑]] : 日露戦争の戦死者のために建てられた。題字の揮毫は[[乃木希典]]{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.1}}。 ; 頌徳碑 : 財団法人帝国在郷軍人会の創立者である松本謄四郎を顕彰した碑。当初は旭ヶ丘にあったが、[[1960年]]（昭和35年）3月、当社に移設された{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.11}}。 : 松本を称える正面の碑文は、[[佐藤昌介]]の撰による。[[1967年]]（昭和42年）、右側面に在郷軍人会の遺族を慰霊する文が刻字された{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.11}}。 ; 尼港殉難碑 : [[尼港事件]]の犠牲者のための碑。[[1928年]]（昭和3年）10月、旭ヶ丘に建てられたが、1960年（昭和35年）3月5日、当社に移設された{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.15}}。 ; ノモンハン英魂之碑 : [[ノモンハン事件]]の犠牲者のための碑。1967年（昭和42年）9月16日建立。[[1987年]]（昭和62年）にはアフリカ産黒御影石製の由来碑が添えられた{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.36}}。 ; アッツ島玉砕 雄魂之碑 : [[アッツ島の戦い]]での犠牲者のための碑。[[1968年]]（昭和43年）7月29日建立。幅7メートルの台座の上に、32トンの神居古潭石製の碑が載る{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.42}}。 ; メレヨン島戦没者慰霊碑 : [[ウォレアイ環礁]]での犠牲者のための碑。[[1971年]]（昭和46年）10月建立。黒御影石製で、題字は[[堂垣内尚弘]]による。左後方には戦没者の氏名碑が立つ{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.48}}。 ; 北千島慰霊碑 : [[千島列島#分類|北千島]]での犠牲者のための碑。[[1975年]]（昭和50年）8月23日建立。日高産碑原石製で、題字は堂垣内尚弘による{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.54}}。 ; 北海道全海軍 英魂の碑 : 北海道・千島・樺太にゆかりのあるすべての海軍関係者のための碑。[[1978年]]（昭和53年）8月20日建立。重巡洋艦で使われていた錨2基を配する{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.56}}。 ; 「北鎮砲兵発祥の地」碑 : [[1896年]]（明治29年）12月に結成された独立野戦砲大隊を記念する碑。[[1985年]]（昭和60年）6月23日建立。アフリカ産黒御影石製で、題字は[[板垣武四]]による{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.63}}。 ; 旭川第七連隊砲兵哨舎 :「北鎮砲兵発祥の地」碑建立の数年前に自衛隊が運んできたもの{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.63}}。 ; 歩兵第26連隊軍旗奉焼の碑 : [[歩兵第26連隊]]の解散に伴い、[[月寒神社]]で行われた軍旗奉焼を記念する碑。[[1986年]]（昭和61年）9月14日建立。白御影石製で、沿革碑が添えられている{{Sfn|吉岡|loc=No.66}}。 == ギャラリー == File:Monument to the Imperilal Visit at Sapporo Gokoku {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012.
