{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo|qq=}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hokkaido|qq=}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrines|qq=}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kojun|qq=}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairakuen (Sapporo)|qq=}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogi Maresuke|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikolaevsk Incident|qq=}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Khalkhin Gol|qq=}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Attu|qq=}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Woleai Atoll|qq=}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dokaiguchi Takahiro|qq=}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuril Islands|qq=}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo|qq=}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hokkaido|qq=}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrines|qq=}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kojun|qq=}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairakuen (Sapporo)|qq=}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogi Maresuke|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikolaevsk Incident|qq=}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Khalkhin Gol|qq=}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Attu|qq=}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Woleai Atoll|qq=}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dokaiguchi Takahiro|qq=}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuril Islands|qq=}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo|qq=}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hokkaido|qq=}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrines|qq=}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kojun|qq=}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairakuen (Sapporo)|qq=}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogi Maresuke|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikolaevsk Incident|qq=}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Khalkhin Gol|qq=}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Attu|qq=}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Woleai Atoll|qq=}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dokaiguchi Takahiro|qq=}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuril Islands|qq=}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kojun|qq=}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairakuen (Sapporo)|qq=}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogi Maresuke|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikolaevsk Incident|qq=}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Khalkhin Gol|qq=}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Attu|qq=}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Woleai Atoll|qq=}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dokaiguchi Takahiro|qq=}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuril Islands|qq=}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ({{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, {{ill|Sapporo|ja|札幌市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo|qq=}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|ja|北海道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hokkaido|qq=}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|ja|護国神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrines|qq=}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|lt=Taga-taisha|lt=Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}}, and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}}. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|lt=Taga-taisha|lt=Taga Taisha|ja|多賀大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Taisha|qq=}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}} and {{ill|Empress Kojun|ja|香淳皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kojun|qq=}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|ja|屯田兵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondenhei|qq=}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|ja|西南戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma Rebellion|qq=}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairakuen (Sapporo)|ja|偕楽園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairakuen (Sapporo)|qq=}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|ja|乃木希典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogi Maresuke|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolaevsk Incident|ja|尼港事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikolaevsk Incident|qq=}}. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battle of Khalkhin Gol|ja|ノモンハン事件|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Khalkhin Gol|qq=}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|ja|アッツ島の戦い|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Attu|qq=}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai Atoll|ja|ウォレアイ環礁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Woleai Atoll|qq=}}. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Dokaiguchi Takahiro|ja|堂垣内尚弘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dokaiguchi Takahiro|qq=}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|ja|千島列島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuril Islands|qq=}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmangu Omikami|qq=}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama-tsumi no Kami|qq=}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmangu Omikami|qq=}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=}} ** As of [[2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == * [[1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=}} in [[1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=}}. In [[1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the visit of Emperor and Empress Showa File:Neushi Stone.JPG|Neushi Stone File:Monument of Sakura Tree Planting at Shotokuen.JPG|Sakura Tree Planting Monument File:Monument of Shotokuen.JPG|Entrance to
