{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of [[:en:2011|2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of [[:en:2011|2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|qq=|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of [[:en:2011|2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|qq=|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|qq=|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|qq=|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|qq=|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|qq=|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = [[:en:1879|1879]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]] 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = [[:en:July 6|July 6]] |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Japan|Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[:en:Yasukuni Shrine|Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[:en:Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, [[:en:Sapporo|Sapporo]], [[:en:Hokkaido|Hokkaido]]. It is one of the [[:en:Gokoku shrines|Gokoku shrines]], dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]], and in [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of [[:en:2011|2011]] (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q813858}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナミ|1=Izanami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q682306}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * [[:en:1879|1879]] (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]] was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * [[:en:1911|1911]] (Meiji 44) – Moved to [[:en:Nakajima Park|Nakajima Park]]. * [[:en:1922|1922]] (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * [[:en:1939|1939]] (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * [[:en:1946|1946]] (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * [[:en:1949|1949]] (Showa 24) – Deities from [[:en:Taga-taisha|Taga Taisha]] were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * [[:en:1968|1968]] (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * [[:en:1970|1970]] (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * [[:en:1971|1971]] (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * [[:en:1972|1972]] (Showa 47) – [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]] and [[:en:Empress Nagako|Empress Kojun]] visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in [[:en:1878|1878]] (Meiji 11) to honor the [[:en:Tondenhei|Tondenhei]] who died in the [[:en:Satsuma Rebellion|Satsuma Rebellion]]. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in [[:en:Kairaku-en|Kairakuen (Sapporo)]], it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in [[:en:1907|1907]] (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] in the Sapporo regiment district. In [[:en:1933|1933]] (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General [[:en:Nogi Maresuke|Nogi Maresuke]].{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In [[:en:1967|1967]] (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the [[:en:Nikolayevsk incident|Nikolaevsk Incident]]. Built in [[:en:1928|1928]] (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in [[:en:1960|1960]] (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the [[:en:Battles of Khalkhin Gol|Battle of Khalkhin Gol]]. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in [[:en:1987|1987]] (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the [[:en:Battle of Attu|Battle of Attu]]. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the [[:en:Woleai|Woleai Atoll]]. Built in [[:en:October 1971|October 1971]] (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by [[:en:Naohiro Dōgakinai|Dokaiguchi Takahiro]]. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the [[:en:Kuril Islands|Kuril Islands]]. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the
