{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of {{ill|2011|en|2011|WD=Q1994|lt=2011}} (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the '''Taga Hall'''
{{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q813858}}

{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q386563}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmangu Omikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of {{ill|2011|en|2011|WD=Q1994|lt=2011}} (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q813858}} * {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナミ|1=Izanami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q682306}} * {{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q813858}}
{{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那美大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナミ|1=Izanami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q682306}}
{{ill|Amaterasu Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}
{{ill|Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q386563}}
{{ill|Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmangu Omikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}}
{{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Dead|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Martyrs of Public Service|ja|公共殉職deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martyrs of Public Service|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Special Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of {{ill|2011|en|2011|WD=Q1994|lt=2011}} (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Taga Hall * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊邪那岐大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|1=Izanagi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q813858}} * Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War Deities|ja|其他特殊deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special Deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ** As of {{ill|2011|en|2011|WD=Q1994|lt=2011}} (Heisei 23), the main hall enshrines 25,543 spirits. ; Omikami|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Omikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Oyama-tsumi no Kami|ja|大山祗大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} * {{ill|Tenjin (kami)|lt=Tenmangu Omikami|ja|天満宮大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja|北海道開拓deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deities of Hokkaido Pioneers|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Spirits of War Dead|ja|各戦役戦没deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirits of War (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} * {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} == History == * {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido – A monument to the spirits of the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}} was erected at what is now Kita 6-jo Nishi 7-chome, Sapporo, and the site was named '''Sapporo Chukonsha'''. * {{ill|1911|en|1911|WD=Q2076|lt=1911}} (Meiji 44) – Moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|en|Nakajima Park|WD=Q5371866|lt=Nakajima Park}}. * {{ill|1922|en|1922|WD=Q2165|lt=1922}} (Taisho 11) – Renamed '''Sapporo Shokonsha'''. * {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8) – A new shrine was built at its current location. * {{ill|1939|en|1939|WD=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) – Renamed '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' and designated as a Gokoku Shrine by the Ministry of Home Affairs.[http://www.hokkaidojinjacho.jp/data/01/01009.html Sapporo Gokoku Shrine] – Hokkaido Shrine Association, accessed October 2, 2012. * {{ill|1946|en|1946|WD=Q18610|lt=1946}} (Showa 21) ''' April 30 – Became affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. ''' December 12 – Temporarily renamed '''Sapporo Shotoku Shrine'''. The original name was restored after Japan regained sovereignty. * {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24) – Deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}} were enshrined, and the Taga Hall was built. * {{ill|1968|en|1968|WD=Q2644|lt=1968}} (Showa 43) – A fire destroyed the shrine building. * {{ill|1970|en|1970|WD=Q2474|lt=1970}} (Showa 45) – The shrine was rebuilt. * {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46) – Deities from {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}} were enshrined in the Taga Hall. * {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (Showa 47) – {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Showa}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|en|Empress Nagako|WD=Q230697|lt=Empress Kojun}} visited and prayed. == Shotokuen == A corner of the shrine grounds contains the "Shotokuen," a memorial area featuring numerous monuments centered around a cenotaph for war dead. ; Tondenhei Memorial Monument : Built in {{ill|1878|en|1878|WD=Q7776|lt=1878}} (Meiji 11) to honor the {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. It is believed to be the oldest surviving monument in Sapporo.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} : Initially located in {{ill|Kairaku-en|en|Kairaku-en|WD=Q71952|lt=Kairakuen (Sapporo)}}, it was moved to {{ill|Nakajima Park|ja|中島遊園地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakajima Park|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 中島公園|1=Nakajima Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5371866}} in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (Meiji 40) to include war dead from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|WD=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}} in the Sapporo regiment district. In {{ill|1933|en|1933|WD=Q18726|lt=1933}} (Showa 8), it was relocated to the shrine grounds.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; {{ill|monument to the loyal dead|ja|忠魂碑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/monument to the loyal dead|1=monument to the loyal dead|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11274518}} : A monument for the war dead of the Russo-Japanese War. The inscription was penned by General {{ill|Nogi Maresuke|en|Nogi Maresuke|WD=Q468122|lt=Nogi Maresuke}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.1}} ; Shotoku Monument : A monument honoring Toshiro Matsumoto, the founder of the {{ill|Imperial Veterans' Association|ja|帝国在郷軍人会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Veterans' Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 在郷軍人会|1=Imperial Veterans' Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423997}}. Originally located in Asahigaoka, it was moved to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} : The inscription on the front was composed by {{ill|Sato Shohaku|ja|佐藤昌介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sato Shohaku|1=Satō Shōsuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11384086}}. In {{ill|1967|en|1967|WD=Q2648|lt=1967}} (Showa 42), an additional inscription on the side commemorated the association’s bereaved families.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.11}} ; Niko Incident Monument : A memorial for victims of the {{ill|Nikolayevsk incident|en|Nikolayevsk incident|WD=Q700134|lt=Nikolaevsk Incident}}. Built in {{ill|1928|en|1928|WD=Q19715|lt=1928}} (Showa 3) in Asahigaoka, it was relocated to the shrine in {{ill|1960|en|1960|WD=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.15}} ; Nomonhan Heroic Souls Monument : A memorial for the dead of the {{ill|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|en|Battles of Khalkhin Gol|WD=Q188925|lt=Battle of Khalkhin Gol}}. Built on [[September 16, 1967]] (Showa 42). A supplementary plaque made of African black granite was added in {{ill|1987|en|1987|WD=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62).{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.36}} ; Attu Island Monument : A memorial for the {{ill|Battle of Attu|en|Battle of Attu|WD=Q700572|lt=Battle of Attu}}. Built on [[July 29, 1968]] (Showa 43). It features a 32-ton monument made of stone from {{ill|Kamuikotan|ja|神居古潭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamuikotan|1=Kamuikotan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11589515}} on a seven-meter-wide base.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.42}} ; Mereyon Island Cenotaph : A memorial for the dead in the {{ill|Woleai|en|Woleai|WD=Q567984|lt=Woleai Atoll}}. Built in {{ill|October 1971|en|October 1971|WD=Q7076894|lt=October 1971}} (Showa 46). The monument is made of black granite and includes inscriptions by {{ill|Naohiro Dōgakinai|en|Naohiro Dōgakinai|WD=Q11427859|lt=Dokaiguchi Takahiro}}. A plaque listing the names of the deceased stands nearby.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.48}} ; Northern Kurils Cenotaph : A monument for the dead in the {{ill|Kuril Islands|en|Kuril Islands|WD=Q80389|lt=Kuril Islands}}. Built on [[August 23, 1975]] (Showa 50). The main stone comes from Hidaka, with the inscription penned by Dokaiguchi Takahiro.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.54}} ; Monument to Hokkaido Naval War Dead : A memorial dedicated to all naval personnel connected to Hokkaido, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin. Built on [[August 20, 1978]] (Showa 53). It features two anchors from a heavy cruiser.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.56}} ; "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" Monument : A memorial commemorating the independent field artillery battalion established in [[December 1896]] (Meiji 29). Built on [[June 23, 1985]] (Showa 60). The monument is made of African black granite, with the inscription penned by {{ill|Itagaki Takeji|ja|板垣武四|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itagaki Takeji|1=Takeshi Itagaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11532564}}.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; Asahikawa 7th Regiment Artillery Sentry Box : A sentry box brought by the Self-Defense Forces prior to the construction of the "Birthplace of the Northern Artillery" monument.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.63}} ; 26th Infantry Regiment Flag Burning Memorial : A monument commemorating the burning of the regimental flag of the {{ill|26th Infantry Regiment|ja|歩兵第26連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/26th Infantry Regiment|1=26th Infantry Regiment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11123681}} during its dissolution at {{ill|Tsukisamu Shrine|ja|月寒神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukisamu Shrine|qq=}}. Built on [[September 14, 1986]] (Showa 61). Made of white granite, the monument includes a historical plaque.{{Sfn|Yoshioka|loc=No.66}} == Gallery == File:Monument to the Imperial Visit at Sapporo Gokoku Shrine.JPG|Monument commemorating the {{ill|Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja|耳早立雄大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimi-hayataka-no-O-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} |Shrine Rank = |Establishment = {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} 12) |Main hall = |Other name = |festival = {{ill|July 6|en|July 6|WD=Q2695|lt=July 6}} |Rituals = }} {{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.{{Cite web |last=Guide |first=Hokkaido |date=2018-05-25 |title=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine |url=https://hokkaidoguide.com/sapporo-gokoku-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Hokkaido Guide}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Shōkonsha|en|Shōkonsha|WD=Q11497810|lt=Shokonsha}} in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} '''Sapporo Gokoku Shrine''' ({{ill|Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|ja|札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, {{OldFont|'''札幌護國神󠄀社󠄁'''}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|ja|中央区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chuo Ward (Sapporo)|1=Chūōku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q20652290}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo}}, {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|WD=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}}. It is one of the {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|WD=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku shrines}}, dedicated to spirits of those who died in war. The shrine was established in {{ill|1879|en|1879|WD=Q7783|lt=1879}} (Meiji 12) to enshrine the spirits of {{ill|Tondenhei|en|Tondenhei|WD=Q11465766|lt=Tondenhei}} who died in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|WD=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}. Since then, it has enshrined the spirits of war dead from various conflicts. In {{ill|1949|en|1949|WD=Q5188|lt=1949}} (Showa 24), the shrine began enshrining deities from {{ill|Taga-taisha|en|Taga-taisha|WD=Q402091|lt=Taga Taisha}}, and in {{ill|1971|en|1971|WD=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), it incorporated the deities of the former {{ill|Yamahana Shrine|ja|山鼻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamahana Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 札幌護国神社|1=Sapporo Gokoku Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11521480}}.[http://www3.ocn.ne.jp/~gokoku30/goannnai1.htm Shrine Introduction] – Sapporo Gokoku Shrine official website, accessed October 2, 2012. The shrine consists of the original main shrine and the '''Taga Hall''', which houses deities added later. == Deities == ; main hall * {{ill|Deities of Hokkaido (kami)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天満大自在天神|1=Tenjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1753428}} *
